name: John Mark
bio: John, surnamed Mark, son of Mary in whose Jerusalem house the church gathered to pray during Peter's imprisonment, accompanied Barnabas and Saul when they returned to Antioch after their relief mission (Acts 12:12, 25). His further role alongside Paul and Barnabas, and tradition crediting him as the author of the Gospel of Mark, are told in detail in the chapters ahead. He accompanied Barnabas and Saul as their minister on the voyage to Cyprus, but left them at Perga to return to Jerusalem rather than continuing on into Pisidia (Acts 13:5, 13). When Barnabas later wanted to bring him along on a return visit to the churches, Paul refused because Mark had deserted them in Pamphylia; the disagreement split Paul and Barnabas apart, and Barnabas took Mark with him to Cyprus instead (Acts 15:36-39). Paul's letter to the Colossians identifies him as the son of Barnabas's sister, and commends him to their hospitality if he should visit (Colossians 4:10).
